chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ibn Abu Yafour, who said:

Khattab al-Juhani used to mix with us and was extremely hostile to the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), and he was a companion of Najdat al-Haruriyya. I said: So I visited him to recover from the mixing and dissimulation, and behold, he was unconscious at the threshold of death. I heard him saying: 'What is the matter with me and you, O Ali?' So I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He saw him, by the Lord of the Ka'bah! He saw him, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Dissimulation (practicing concealment of faith or feelings to avoid harm)
key_terms.خَطَّابٌ الْجُهَنِيُّ: Khattab al-Juhani, a specific companion known for his enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.رَبِّ الْكَعْبَةِ: The Lord of the Ka'bah (an oath used by the Imams)
key_terms.نَجْدَةَ الْحَرُورِيَّةَ: Najdat al-Haruriyya, a leader of the Khawarij sect

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Khattab al-Juhani's final words 'What is the matter with me and you, O Ali?'
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the phenomenon of *al-Ru'ya* (vision) at the hour of death, where Khattab al-Juhani, a staunch partisan of the Khawarij, experiences a spiritual awakening amidst his enmity. Imam al-Sadiq’s emphatic confirmation that he 'saw' the Prophet indicates a moment of divine recognition or revelation of truth before his soul departs, serving as a key example of how believers and disbelievers perceive the unseen at their final moments.
